title: Catholic funerals and bands, St. Catherine church
summary: Catholic churches stopped using bands; Henry recalls burying people from St. Catherine and George McCullum with the Tuxedo.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Now what about the different churches here in the city, like Methodists and Baptists and Catholics? How long would the funerals last for them?

Well, they see nothing at all. In other words, they're Catholics, and they wouldn't... They see, they used no band now, they didn't. But by the time back, we used to play for them, but they don't use no band at all. They're not Catholic.
About when was that rule came out about the Catholics?
Well, I couldn't exactly say, but it hasn't been too long. It's been a little while ago.
Before the Depression, or after? After the Depression. After 1929.
Because I see the time, I used to go to the church there on the Tudin Avenue. Yeah, the church there.
I know the one, you mean, out around Galvez?
No, around the... Across from the charity?
You buried people from that church? I buried people from that church.
Was that before World War II? Yeah.
Yeah, I believe it was before. It's been a pretty good while. Because I remember the George, this place, the George McCunty. Yeah. The trumpet player.
What band was that? The Tuxedo. Well, you could check on that through the church records.
I was thinking, yeah. I would show you that. And the church records are showing that. Was it cut out?
